newsitem.title: USA: IBM says remains on track for full year.
newsitem.headline: IBM says remains on track for full year.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp's interim chief financial officer on Monday said he was pleased with the company's second-quarter results and "comfortable" about the rest of the year.

"We feel good about second quarter," Lawrence Ricciardi told analysts in a conference call. "We remain comfortable about the year because of our balanced portfolio. We are performing in line with our long-term objectives."
Ricciardi said he is a proponent of share buybacks, as was his predecessor, G. Richard Thoman.

"I was commenting on my general sense of the business climate," Ricciardi said in a brief interview after the conference call, adding that he would not comment on analysts' estimates for the full year.
"The analysts' models belong to the analysts," he said. According to First Call, analysts expect IBM to earn $5.70 to $6.35 a share in 1997, with a consensus estimate of $6.18.

In his review of IBM's business units, Ricciardi said IBM was not satisfied with the performance of the RS/6000 workstation business, though he was "feeling better about the story" at the company's AS/400 minicomputer business.
At the personal computer unit, he said IBM's quarterly growth rate fell behind rival Compaq Computer Corp's.

"As opposed to last quarter, Compaq grew faster than we did in both in units and revenue," he said. "In gross profit margin they maintained their lead; in expense-to-revenue we maintained our lead; and inventory turnover was a toss-up."
IBM hired 4,000 new staff in the quarter at its rapidly growing services business, he said. IBM's services backlog stands at $36 billion, with new contract signings totaling more than $3 billion.

With respect to second-quarter results, Ricciardi said IBM's efforts to cut its tax burden, such as by moving disk drive manufacturing to lower-tax locations, offset the effect of currency exchange rate fluctuations during the quarter.
"Our tax work helped our EPS by about $0.10 in the second quarter," he said. "That basically offset the currency hit which coincidentally was precisely $0.10 a share."
Ricciardi also commented briefly on IBM's efforts to find a permanent chief financial officer, saying the search involved candidates from inside and outside the company.
